findings.title: Isolate fixture Git commands from the caller’s repository
findings.body: The new tests run `git init`, `config`, `add`, `commit`, `checkout`, and `update-ref` with the caller’s environment. An absolute `GIT_DIR` or `GIT_INDEX_FILE` inherited from a hook can redirect those writes into the developer’s repository despite `cwd=repo`. The fixture can overwrite the real index or refs during `make test`. `scripts/test_install_gates_runtime.py` already clears these variables for its fixtures.

findings.title: Fail closed when Git cannot enumerate changes
findings.body: A failed Git command becomes an empty path list. I confirmed that pointing `--repo` at an existing non-repository directory produces a successful empty plan. A failed committed, staged, or unstaged diff inside a real checkout likewise drops that portion of the candidate and allows the remaining checks to report success.

findings.title: Bind discovery to the repository named by `--repo`
findings.body: `git -C` still honors inherited `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, and `GIT_INDEX_FILE`. If those identify another clean checkout, the selector can discover zero changes there and skip every test for the requested dirty checkout. The existing shared Git surface gate has a regression test for this exact redirection.

findings.title: Require a trustworthy base when integration refs are unavailable
findings.body: In a single-branch clone containing several feature commits and none of the three named integration refs, the fallback compares only the last commit. A hook change followed by a documentation commit selects tests for the documentation alone. In a depth-one checkout, even the last commit disappears from discovery.

findings.title: Keep unpublished local integration commits in the candidate
findings.body: If local `main` is one unpublished hook commit ahead of `origin/main`, a feature branched from it with one documentation commit chooses local `main` as the nearest base. A PR to `origin/main` contains both commits, but the local plan omits the hook suite. Running directly on the ahead local `main` can produce a completely empty plan.

findings.title: Pass the resolved base to all base-sensitive gates
findings.body: `--base-ref main` can resolve and discover the right files, yet the shared Git surface gate still receives `--default-base-ref origin/dev`. In a clone without `origin/dev`, execution fails before reaching the suites. Where both refs exist, metadata and release checks can judge a different range. Suites such as `test_frozen_case_sanctity.sh` also skip their base-relative assertions unless `CCL_SKILL_BASE_REF` reaches them.

findings.title: Include code-review shards in the full fallback
findings.body: The fallback runs only repository gates and fast regressions. If a mapped code-review suite is renamed and the Makefile points to its replacement, escalation never runs the replacement shard, even with `FULL=1`. The same omission applies to an unknown path that affects code-review behavior.

findings.title: Preserve missing suite registrations until drift is checked
findings.body: Deleting `hooks/test_agy_bridge.py` while leaving its Makefile recipe removes the suite from `makefile_suites()` before `add_suite()` can record it as missing. The hook fallback can finish without reporting drift, while `make test-repo-gates` will fail on the missing file. The fallback coverage test derives its expected set through the same filter.

findings.title: Run repository-wide content gates across their actual input domains
findings.body: A tracked change to `scripts/install.sh` can introduce private provenance or a broken backticked spec citation. Both `check-public-sanitization.py` and `check-spec-references.py` scan tracked source files, but this path selects neither. Their CI checks can fail after the affected run reports success.

findings.title: Account for the checks that cannot see untracked files
findings.body: A new untracked `docs/guide.md` is included in `changed_files`, but the Markdown link checker, spec checker, document linter, and sanitization gate enumerate tracked files. An invalid link or private value in that document can receive an `ok` result and turn red immediately after `git add`, without any content change.

findings.title: Include integration consumers of shared hook helpers
findings.body: `hooks/guard-edit-isolation.sh` invokes `host-input.py paths`, and `test_guard_edit_isolation.sh` exercises the resulting edit decisions. Changing the helper never selects that suite or its installed-runtime test. The same dependency gap affects `skill-loading.py`, which `test_agy_bridge.py` loads directly, and `merge-authorization-prompt.sh`, which `test_guard_merge_authorization.sh` exercises with the guard.

findings.title: Route evaluation fixtures to the tests that read them
findings.body: Changing `eval/routing-tasks.jsonl` selects body-compliance and general evaluation tests but omits `test_routing_bank_integrity.sh` and `test_frozen_case_sanctity.sh`. A duplicate case ID or an unadjudicated change to a frozen expectation can escape. A broken oracle under `eval/paired-tasks/` similarly misses `test_skill_paired_eval.py`, which checks the committed tasks.

findings.title: Schedule abort-leak probes when their fixture changes
findings.body: `test_review_gate_abort_leak.sh` runs `test_review_gate.sh` and checks what happens when its controller is interrupted. Changing the fixture’s cleanup or hang bound selects only the ordinary suite, even with `FULL=1`. The ordinary run can finish successfully while the interrupted run leaves a wrapper alive.

findings.title: Select npm checks for every packaged runtime input
findings.body: `build-assets.mjs` packages `.antigravity-plugin`, root `hooks.json`, `agent-context`, `skills`, and `scripts/owner-dispatch`, among other inputs. Changing only `.antigravity-plugin/plugin.json` never sets `npm_required`, even with `--with-npm --include-slow`. Adding a forbidden version field therefore skips the npm test that explicitly rejects it.

findings.title: Read Git path output as NUL-delimited filesystem names
findings.body: With Git’s default quoting, a changed `hooks/test_路由.py` is returned as quoted, escaped text. It no longer matches `hooks/` or the suite filename, so its self-test is lost. Line splitting, whitespace stripping, and converting literal backslashes to slashes also change valid POSIX filenames before selection.

findings.title: Check Git metadata even when the tree diff is empty
findings.body: An empty commit, or a change followed by a revert, can leave no changed paths while introducing a prohibited commit message or author identity. The early return skips `shared_git_surface_gate.py`, although the gate checks the candidate’s commits and branch name independently of file contents.

findings.title: Check whitespace in the committed and staged candidate
findings.body: After staging a line with trailing whitespace, plain `git diff --check` sees an empty unstaged diff. The same happens after committing the line. Discovery includes both kinds of change, but the advertised whitespace preflight checks neither.

findings.title: Select CI wiring tests for their configuration inputs
findings.body: Removing `pyyaml` from `requirements-test.txt` selects four suites that do not check the dependency declaration. `test_check_spec_references.py` explicitly checks both required dependencies, the workflow install steps, the Makefile gate invocation, and the contributor instructions. Changes to those inputs can bypass the corresponding assertions locally.

findings.title: Run the skill-count gate when either README changes
findings.body: `check-skill-count.py` reads both `README.md` and `packages/ccl-skills-npm/README.md`. Editing either stated count alone leaves `need_skill_count` false. A stale public count can pass locally and fail the CI skill-count gate.

findings.title: Route obligation evidence to its repository audit
findings.body: Changing only `specs/065-uiux-evidence-delivery/obligation-mapping.jsonl` takes the generic `specs/` branch. It skips `test_obligation_ledger_repo_audit.sh`, which reads that exact mapping and ledger. A mismatched carrier hash can therefore escape the affected run.

findings.title: Select contract tests for the skill prose they inspect
findings.body: Editing `skills/product-ui-ux-design/references/delivery-contract.md` omits `test_uiux_delivery_contract.sh`, which reads and checks the actual document. The same routing gap skips `test_routing_pointer_integrity.sh` for entrypoints whose triggers it pins, and skips `test-public-data-acquisition-recipes.sh` when the executable examples it extracts from Markdown change.

findings.title: Include code-review wrapper tests for shared parser changes
findings.body: `concern_excerpt.py` feeds the Claude and OpenCode wrappers, whose probe and retry suites assert the emitted diagnostic fields. Its mapping runs only the helper suite. Conversely, `test_concern_excerpt.sh` checks the actual wiring in `claude_review.sh` and `parse_cli_review.py`, but changes to either consumer omit that test.

findings.title: Derive the core code-review fanout from the registered shards
findings.body: Adding a suite to either Makefile code-review shard does not add it to `CODE_REVIEW_SHARD_SUITES`. A later change to `review_gate.py` silently skips that suite. The literal-path drift test still passes because every path already present in the copied list exists.

findings.title: Apply slow-lane policy before adding self-tests to the parallel runner
findings.body: Changing `test_review_gate_abort_leak.sh` puts the probe in `parallel_suites` before the slow-lane rule runs. The default plan says the probe was skipped while actually launching it alongside other suites, contrary to its dedicated-runner requirement. With `FULL=1`, it runs there and then repeats in the serial legs.

findings.title: Treat an unavailable Docker daemon as an incomplete sandbox check
findings.body: With the Docker CLI installed and its daemon stopped, `shutil.which("docker")` succeeds. The selected sandbox suite prints `SKIP` and exits zero unless `VERIFY_SANDBOX_REQUIRE_DOCKER=1` is set. The selector then prints `select_affected_tests_ok` although no sandbox invariant ran.

findings.title: Preserve interim preflight results in the final status
findings.body: `check-ccl-skills.sh` deliberately exits zero with `ccl_skill_check_interim_ok` when checks such as the private R0 audit were unavailable. The selector reads only the exit code and its own planned skips, then emits an unconditional `ok`. A consumer reading the final status loses the distinction the gate requires.

findings.title: Validate dependency changes against the candidate npm lockfile
findings.body: If `node_modules` already exists, even `--with-npm` skips `npm ci`. A change that makes `package.json` inconsistent with the lockfile can pass against the previously installed tree and fail immediately in the clean CI installation.

findings.title: Keep automatically executed suites inside the checkout
findings.body: `is_file()` follows symlinks, and `--files` accepts `..` components. A changed `test_*.sh` symlink, or an accidentally parent-relative explicit path, can make the parallel runner execute a script outside the repository with the developer’s permissions.

findings.title: Render dry-run commands with shell-safe argument boundaries
findings.body: A suite path containing a space is one argument during execution but two arguments in the printed command. Shell metacharacters in a filename can also become active if the preview is copied into a shell. The preview additionally omits the requested `--jobs`, so it cannot reproduce the actual invocation.

findings.title: Use each Python suite’s actual test runner
findings.body: The self-suite rule sends every `test_*.py` to a runner that invokes `python3 file.py`. A new pytest-style module with a failing test and no `__main__` block exits zero without collecting any tests. The existing report suite avoids this only because a separate hard-coded serial command invokes pytest for it.

findings.title: Cover deletion of registered suites outside the hook map
findings.body: Deleting a registered extraction regression such as `test_validate_skill_cross_refs.sh` silently drops the changed suite. The selected registration self-test checks for *existing unregistered* files, so it does not catch a registered filename that disappeared. The full fast runner will fail when it tries to launch that file.

findings.title: Avoid scheduling the same work through both direct and aggregate commands
findings.body: Changing `test_check_ccl_regressions.sh` runs its default fast lane as a parallel self-test and then runs the same lane serially with `--fast`. Changing `eval/design-judge.py` similarly runs `test_design_judge.py` directly and again via `unittest`. These duplicates defeat the incremental target’s runtime objective.

findings.title: Exercise drift escalation and command execution in the regression tests
findings.body: The escalation test stops after inspecting `_PlanBuilder.missing_suites`, so deleting the full-fallback scheduling would leave it green. Likewise, `test_cli_json_dry_run_and_execution_on_synthetic_suite` invokes only `--json`. Dropping runner execution or swallowing a failing suite’s exit status would leave that test green too.
